[quote=corzerran;61473316]He nodded. [i]"Of course."[/i]

Zachariasz walked beside Elena in quietness for a few moments before starting. [i]"If the vote of the governors accepts it, what will happen? Will you be bound to the draft or will it be up to your discretion?"[/i][/quote]
She paused before answering, [i]"It depends, like anything,"[/i] she waved her hand in front of her as if grasping for what to say [i]"Maybe they all vote yes, and they have the force to back up their decision- it won't be up to my discretion then."[/i]

[i]"But I doubt that's where the strong-arming will start. Bruzhnikoyya isn't working alone, and when he shows his hand to scare me, I'll have the chance to learn more."[/i]

[i]"The force?"[/i] The king took a moment. [i]"Unless I am mistaken, you are the highest commander of the armed forces. Perhaps the governors have command over regional law enforcement, but those officers would still answer to [b]you[/b]. It may not look prim and proper, but if it is a matter of force, you will surely win."[/i]

[i]"And then there is the issue of public perception"[/i] Zachariasz paused for a moment, in thought. [i]"If you are clever enough, which I believe you most certainly are, there is always a way to maintain popular support. The words used are different for all rulers, the situation, and the desired effect of the message. But, ultimately, I believe that if you believe that the governor is strongarming you, there must be [b]some[/b] ulterior motive."[/i] He took a breath. [i]"You have led a successful revolution against a tyrannical government and have placed in its stead one which people are treated well. It is most likely a governor working in good faith and with suitable wisdom would not desire to change the new system."[/i]
